name: Taiwan
description: Taiwan is a highly appealing destination for expats, offering an exceptional quality of life, a robust technology sector, and a welcoming environment. It seamlessly blends modern infrastructure with rich cultural traditions, making it an attractive choice for professionals, students, and retirees seeking a safe and dynamic place to live.
longdescription: Expat life in Taiwan is consistently rated highly due to its high quality of life, friendly locals, and efficient public services. The island boasts a strong economy, particularly in the semiconductor industry, although the broader job market for foreigners outside of tech and English teaching can be somewhat limited. Taiwan's culture is a fascinating mix of Chinese, Japanese, Southeast Asian, and indigenous influences, known for its politeness, hospitality, and vibrant culinary scene, especially the famous night markets. Society is generally open and welcoming to foreigners, and the country is considered very safe with low crime rates. Major cities like Taipei, Taichung, and Kaohsiung offer diverse living experiences, from bustling urban centers to more laid-back atmospheres with affordable rents. The cost of living is generally lower than in many Western and other East Asian capitals, particularly for food and public transportation, contributing to its appeal as an economical yet high-quality place to live.

visas.name: Taiwan Employment Gold Card
visas.description: A flexible 4-in-1 card (work permit, residence permit, multi-entry visa, re-entry permit) for foreign professionals in tech, science, arts, or finance, without requiring employer sponsorship.
benefits: Live and work in Taiwan without employer sponsorship
Tax incentives: 50% income tax exemption on salary over NT$3 million
Sponsor residency for spouses and children
Access to Taiwan's world-class National Health Insurance (NHI)
visas.path_to_residency_description: Can apply for permanent residency (APRC) after 3 years (reduced to 2 years for PhD holders).

Citizenship by Descent.desc:
Taiwanese nationality is primarily based on the principle of *jus sanguinis* (by blood). If one or both of your parents are Taiwanese nationals at the time of your birth, you are likely automatically a Taiwanese national.

*   **Key updates as of January 1, 2024:**
    *   Nationals without Household Registration (NWOHR) who were born to at least one parent with active household registration in Taiwan at the time of their birth no longer need to reside in Taiwan for a minimum period before applying for household registration.
    *   This also applies to those born overseas with at least one parent having household registration.
    *   Minors (under 18) with parents holding active Household Registrations can follow a simpler process and proceed directly to Household Registration without needing a Taiwan Area Residence Certificate (TARC).
    *   Individuals adopted by Taiwanese citizens as of January 1, 2024, may also apply for citizenship.

*   **Process for NWOHRs seeking full citizenship (with Household Registration):**
    *   Apply for a Taiwan (NWOHR) passport at a local Taiwanese diplomatic mission.
    *   Enter Taiwan using the NWOHR passport.
    *   (Sometimes) Apply for a Taiwan Area Residence Certificate (TARC) and reside in Taiwan for a specified period (e.g., one year with at least 335 days, two years with at least 270 days/year, or five years with at least 183 days/year) if not covered by the 2024 amendments for direct household registration.
    *   Register for Household Registration to become a full citizen and obtain a National ID card.

Naturalization.desc:
Foreign nationals over the age of 20 may naturalize as Republic of China (ROC) nationals.

*   **General Requirements:**
    *   Resided legally in Taiwan for at least five continuous years, with more than 183 days of physical presence each year.
    *   Must be of good character.
    *   Possess sufficient property or professional skills to make an independent living.
    *   Demonstrate proficiency in Mandarin Chinese. This can be proven by taking a test (70% for standard application) or studying a certain number of hours in a recognized school (200 hours for standard application).
    *   A clean criminal record from the country of origin.
    *   Applicants are typically required to renounce their previous nationalities, though exceptions exist if the home country's law makes this impossible without first acquiring another citizenship.

*   **Process:**
    *   Submit the application for naturalization to the local Household Registration Office.
    *   Upon successful initial application, a Certificate of R.O.C. Naturalization Candidature is issued.
    *   Within one year, renounce original citizenship and provide formal proof.
    *   Receive a Certificate of Naturalization and then apply for a Taiwan Area Residence Certificate (TARC).
    *   Reside for an additional period (e.g., one year for over 335 days, two years for over 270 days/year, or five years for over 183 days/year) before applying for Household Registration to gain full citizen status and an ID card.

Birthright.desc:
Taiwan does not generally grant birthright citizenship (*jus soli*).

*   Children born to foreign national parents in Taiwan are not automatically Taiwanese citizens and typically follow the nationality of their parents.
*   **Exceptions:**
    *   Citizenship is granted if a child of unknown parentage is found within the territory of Taiwan. However, this citizenship can be removed upon legitimization by a foreign parent.
    *   Children born within the Taiwan Area to stateless parents are also granted nationality at birth.

*   **Benefits for those born in Taiwan (not to Taiwanese parents):** Being born in Taiwan can offer certain benefits during the naturalization process, such as being able to apply for naturalization after three consecutive years of residency (compared to the usual five).

Spouse and Family.desc:
The naturalization process is generally easier for spouses of Taiwanese nationals.

*   **Spouse of a Taiwanese National:**
    *   The residency requirement for naturalization is reduced to three years (from five) if married to a Taiwanese citizen, with more than 183 days of physical presence per year.
    *   May be exempted from providing a police criminal record if they already possess an Alien Permanent Resident Certificate or their Alien Resident Certificate states "dependent of relatives (husband or wife)" as the residence reason, or if they were once married to an ROC citizen and have not left Taiwan since the marital relationship ended.
    *   The language proficiency test requirement may also be reduced (e.g., 60% score needed for the test, or 72 hours of study).
    *   If the spouse is a resident of the People's Republic of China (PRC), they can obtain household registration in Taiwan without first acquiring ROC nationality. Spouses who are nationals of other countries need to become naturalized before becoming eligible for household registration.

*   **Children of Naturalized Citizens:**
    *   Unmarried minor children may apply for nationality if a parent acquires nationality by naturalization. A naturalized parent may apply for them on their behalf.
    *   The spouse and non-majority age children of a naturalized citizen can acquire Taiwanese citizenship unless it is contrary to the law of their original country.

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax (IIT):**
    *   **Tax Residents (residing in Taiwan for 183 days or more or having household registration and visiting for at least one day):** Subject to progressive tax rates ranging from 5% to 40% (for tax year 2025). Foreign-sourced income exceeding TWD 1 million is subject to Income Basic Tax (IBT) at a flat rate of 20% if the basic income exceeds TWD 7.5 million.
    *   **Non-residents (residing in Taiwan for less than 183 days):**
        *   If monthly salary exceeds NT$41,205 (1.5x minimum wage for 2025), a flat rate of 18% applies to Taiwan-sourced income.
        *   If monthly salary is NT$41,205 or below, a 6% income tax rate applies.
        *   Remuneration received from an entity registered outside of Taiwan is tax-exempt for non-residents staying less than 90 days.
    *   **Deductions and Exemptions (for tax year 2025):** Personal exemption of NT$97,000, standard deduction of NT$131,000 (single) or NT$262,000 (married), and special deduction for salary or wages up to NT$218,000. Basic living expense deduction is NT$213,000 per person.
    *   **Employment Gold Card Holders:** Qualify for tax concessions, including income assessment on only half of their salary above NT$3 million and exemption from alternative minimum tax for foreign source income for their first five years as a tax resident.
*   **Corporate Income Tax (CIT):**
    *   The standard corporate income tax rate in Taiwan is 20%.
    *   Companies with taxable income of NT$120,000 or less are exempt from CIT.
    *   Resident companies are taxed on their worldwide income. Non-resident companies with a permanent establishment in Taiwan are taxed only on Taiwan-sourced income attributable to the PE.
    *   An additional profit retention tax of 5% is imposed on any current earnings of a resident corporation that remain undistributed by the end of the following year.
    *   Corporate Income Basic Tax (IBT) is 12% for companies with certain tax-exempt income, with a deduction of TWD 600,000 for taxable year 2025.
*   **Value Added Tax (VAT):**
    *   The standard VAT rate in Taiwan is 5%, officially known as "business tax."
    *   A zero rate applies to certain exports and specific supplies.
    *   VAT registration is generally required for businesses carrying out taxable activities in Taiwan; there is no general turnover threshold for domestic businesses. Foreign e-commerce operators providing services to individuals in Taiwan must register if their annual Taiwan sales exceed TWD 480,000 (approximately USD 15,500).
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Taiwan generally offers an affordable cost of living compared to Western countries and other major East Asian cities like Tokyo or Seoul. Rent is significantly lower, especially outside of Taipei. A single expat can live comfortably on €1,200 to €1,800 per month, including housing, food, and transportation.
*   **Language:** Mandarin Chinese is the official language. While many educated Taiwanese, especially in Taipei, speak English, learning some Mandarin is highly recommended for daily life and better integration.
*   **Safety:** Taiwan is considered extremely safe with very low crime rates, even in major cities at night.
*   **Healthcare:** Taiwan boasts a world-class National Health Insurance (NHI) system that is accessible and affordable. Expats holding an Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) must enroll in the NHI after six months of continuous residence, or immediately if employed by a Taiwan-registered company. Private health insurance is recommended for the initial six-month period if not immediately employed.
*   **Registration:** For stays longer than three months, a resident visa is required. Upon arrival, if staying for more than six months, expats must apply for an Alien Resident Certificate (ARC), which serves as an identification card for various processes.
*   **Transportation:** Taiwan has an excellent, efficient, and clean public transportation system, including MRT, buses, and High-Speed Rail, making it easy to travel around the island without a car.
*   **Work Culture:** The work culture in Taiwan can involve longer hours and overtime, which may require an adjustment for some expats.
